clue.text: Drummer perishing in dramatic circumstances

parts.note: a drummer is an old word for a travelling seller drumming up trade, and one dying on stage recalls Arthur Miller's play Death of a ...

explanation.walkthrough: The clue points at Arthur Miller's play whose title is Death of a ..., the death of a commercial traveller (a 'drummer') in a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer is American slang for a travelling commercial representative who drums up orders.

clue.text: Attacked from the air — started with RAF knocking out centre

indicators.note: knocking out centre means the middle letters of started are pushed out by the word before

explanation.surface: An air assault began with the Royal Air Force striking at the heart of things.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of STARTED is ART; RAF knocks it out and takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground targets with low-flying aircraft gunfire.

clue.text: Statesman giving groundsman direction

parts.note: Thomas Lord founded Lord's, the London cricket ground
north is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A politician hands the turf-keeper an instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD is Thomas Lord, whose London cricket ground is named after him; Lord North was British Prime Minister 1770-82.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord North was a Prime Minister during the American War of Independence.

clue.text: Posed in skirts of elegant fabric

parts.note: sat as for a portrait, posed

indicators.note: skirts of means the outside letters of elegant, its edges

explanation.surface: A model sat for a portrait in skirts of a fine material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts of' takes the first and last letters of 'elegant', ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinet is a thin imitation satin cloth.

clue.text: In any case, special unit can provide investment scheme

indicators.note: case means the word any is wrapped around the other letters like a container
special suggests the word unit is rearranged into an unusual form

explanation.surface: Whatever happens, a particular unit can offer a pension plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In any case' reads as the phrase meaning whatever happens, but 'case' is the container signal, with 'special' as the anagram indicator; 'can provide' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuity is a fixed yearly payment bought with a lump sum, a kind of pension investment.

clue.text: Contraption of French failing

parts.note: de is the French word for of
a failing is a moral fault or vice

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a gadget made in France that keeps breaking down.
explanation.definitionFit: A contraption is a mechanical gadget or contrivance, especially an improvised one.

clue.text: Sculptor present before the fifties, getting old

parts.note: to present is to give or donate
L is the Roman fifty, so two fifties give LL

explanation.surface: An artist gives a gift before reaching his fifties and growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' and 'getting' just join the pieces; 'the fifties' gives two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was a Florentine Renaissance sculptor.

clue.text: Essential ingredient I included in main TV broadcast

indicators.note: included in puts the letter inside the shuffled letters
broadcast means the words main TV are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: I appear as a key feature in primetime television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges MAIN TV and 'included in' slots I into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vitamin is an organic compound the body needs in small amounts for health.

clue.text: Instrument Mary found abandoned

explanation.surface: A musical device belonging to a woman who was found deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mary Celeste was a ship found abandoned in the Atlantic in 1872.
explanation.definitionFit: A celeste is a keyboard instrument with hammers striking metal bars; the ghost ship was the Mary Celeste.

clue.text: Hope invention might be apparent in an air I turn out

definitions.note: an adjective for the imaginary kingdom invented by the novelist Anthony Hope in The Prisoner of Zenda

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the words before it are to be put into a different order

explanation.surface: A hopeful new idea might show itself in a tune I produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hope' looks like the ordinary word for optimism but is the novelist Anthony Hope; 'out' rearranges AN AIR I TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Hope created the fictional central European kingdom of Ruritania for his romance novels, so the word belongs to his creation.

clue.text: Relation held back by relation

indicators.note: back means the letters found are read in the opposite direction
held means the letters sit inside the word relation that follows

explanation.surface: A family member is kept at arm's length by another relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' finds ELAT inside 'relation', and 'back' turns those four letters round; the first 'relation' is the definition, in its sense of a telling or account.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation can be a narrative or account, the act of relating a story.

clue.text: Circulate fiscal item in an appropriate place for it

indicators.note: to circulate is to move around, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Pass round a tax document in a suitable publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulate' shuffles FISCAL ITEM IN AN; the newspaper is the right place to print a fiscal item, and a newspaper also circulates.
explanation.definitionFit: A financial news item would naturally appear in the London business daily with pink pages.

clue.text: Girl getting dreadfully hot in boat

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the boat word

parts.note: a dory is a small flat-bottomed fishing boat

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests the word hot is badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A young woman becomes uncomfortably warm while out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: A dory is a small flat-bottomed boat, used in fishing; 'dreadfully' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Little boy and I overcooked lamb, for example

parts.note: Herb is a short form of Herbert

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of over are tampered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A youngster and I left the lamb in the oven too long.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'overcooked' does two jobs as the setter splits it: its first four letters are the fodder and 'cooked' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb eats grass, making it a plant-eating animal.

clue.text: Mistake archbishop in church finally put right

indicators.note: finally put means the last piece is placed at the end
in shows the archbishop sits within the church letters

parts.note: CE is short for Church of England
Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury in the 1930s

explanation.surface: A senior cleric's error in a church is eventually corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: LANG is Cosmo Lang, Archbishop of Canterbury 1928-42; 'finally put' sends R to the end after C(LANG)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A clanger is British slang for a conspicuous blunder, as in dropping a clanger.

clue.text: Material for fruit syrup

explanation.surface: A fabric used for making a fruit cordial.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is both a loosely woven silk fabric and a sweet pomegranate syrup.

clue.text: What's shifted with skill from side to side

indicators.note: shifted means the letters of the word are moved about into another order

parts.note: the word what, with the 's read as is
art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: Someone asks what has been moved skilfully across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifted' is the anagram signal; 'from side to side' is the definition, an old word meaning across.
explanation.definitionFit: Athwart means across, crossing from one side to the other, especially of a ship.

clue.text: Chap promises to repay, without interest

parts.note: Ted is a man's name, so a chap
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A man pledges to pay back the loan with no interest charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without interest' looks financial but means boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tedious is dull and boring, lacking anything to engage you.

clue.text: American city involved with CIA

indicators.note: involved means the letters of with CIA are tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A US town is mixed up with the intelligence agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Wichita is the largest city in Kansas.

clue.text: Give up? That's fine

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to quit and is told that is all right.
explanation.definitionFit: To forfeit is to surrender or lose something; a forfeit is also a penalty such as a fine.

clue.text: Suggestion from Liberal regarded with approval?

indicators.note: regarded with means the letter is held within the approval word, so L is in favour

parts.note: favour is approval or goodwill

explanation.surface: A hint from a Liberal politician received approvingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal is literally 'in favour': L inside FAVOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A flavour of something is a hint or slight trace of it.

clue.text: Bureaucracy reportedly studied record

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: read, past tense, means studied and is pronounced like red
a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: The office paperwork was said to have been examined on file.
explanation.walkthrough: READ in the past tense sounds like RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is excessive official rules and paperwork, named after the ribbon once used to bind documents.

clue.text: Furniture made by high school pupil

parts.note: tall means high
a boy is a schoolboy, a pupil

explanation.surface: Woodwork produced by a secondary-school student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high school' looks like one unit but splits as high and school pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A tallboy is a tall chest of drawers, often in two sections.

clue.text: Abridged history book by Waugh

explanation.surface: A shortened account of the past and a novel by a famous English author.
explanation.walkthrough: Gibbon's History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire is shortened to these words, which are also the title of Evelyn Waugh's first novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibbon's great history is usually called by its short title, and Evelyn Waugh borrowed it for his 1928 satire.

clue.text: Indians one connects with dance

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Native Americans whom one associates with ritual dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'connects with' just joins I after HOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hopi are a Native American people of north-eastern Arizona.

clue.text: In a precarious situation, leg before wicket?

explanation.surface: A batsman in trouble, given out leg before wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, leg before wicket is a way of being dismissed (out) with the ball striking the batsman's leg, a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in an exposed, risky position is the idiom; cryptically a batsman given LBW is dismissed on account of a leg.

clue.text: Lark ad gone for a flight

indicators.note: gone shows that the letters before it disappear from the word for lark

parts.note: a lark is a prank or escapade
the letters ad, dressed up as a dropped-h had

explanation.surface: A cockney says the bird had flown off.
explanation.walkthrough: ''ad gone' reads as Cockney 'had gone', but it tells you to remove AD from ESCAPADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Flight is running away from danger, an act of getting away.

clue.text: Author goes to railway and leaves

parts.note: Graham Greene was an English novelist

explanation.surface: A writer heads for the station and departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb of departing that goes with 'goes', but it is a plural noun meaning foliage; 'goes to' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenery is green foliage, the leaves of plants collectively.
